manifest.purpose: Golden word-level Verilog implementing module recovered_fsm(input clk, input rst, input in, output out) matching interface exactly (all 1-bit ports). Implements a Moore FSM detecting non-overlapping serial pattern '1011' on 'in': uses a 2-bit state register (localparam S0=2'd0 idle/searching '1', S1=2'd1 saw '10', S2=2'd2 saw '101', S3=2'd3 saw '1011'/match) updated in a single always @(posedge clk) block with synchronous active-high reset (rst=1 forces state<-S0 on next edge). Next-state logic via case statement on current state and 'in': S0: in?S1:S0; S1: in?S1:S2; S2: in?S3:S0; S3: in?S1:S0 (non-overlapping restart after match, re-checking last bit appropriately per '1011' overlap semantics). Output 'out' is a Moore output = (state==S3) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0, registered version to align with pattern-detect-then-return-to-search behavior producing exactly one-cycle pulse on completion. No gate primitives instantiated, no textual copy of flattened_netlist.v, no extra ports/signals beyond clk/rst/in/out (all internal signals are local reg/wire declared inside the module, none exposed as ports). Self-contained single-file module compiles standalone with iverilog. This file is the exact answer graded at submission/recovered_rtl.v.
